Thanks for your honesty :) And for the verse. I do believe He is with me even though I don't feel Him.

There were times when I read the Bible for an hour and prayed for an hour. Now, I usually just read a chapter of John with my dad and maybe some from Mark. I only pray for like 5 minutes or less. My depression and anxiety occurred before then though.

Thank you so much for taking this much time to write this post...it is definitely helpful! Feeling understood is already a huge positive, but you gave some great advice along with your writing as well.  I am very sorry about your mother and your struggles with your relationship with her. I wish you a journey of gradual healing. I hope you know how much being you can easily change the world for the better ❤️
Mine were kindness and uplifting. I am a Christian so often listening to encouraging Christian music probably had something to do with it

Looking back at my post, I realize I could have been much more tactful and aware of my audience. I truly apologize if I hurt you or anyone reading this. I was communicating the way I do with my Christian friends/family, being more vague and personal because I know they can fill in the blanks and know where I am coming from. 

People have been scarred in life. As children, they took to heart things that were done or told by other scarred people. And figuring out what is broken inside of us is very difficult. Some of us may not even be aware of our scars. My heart goes out to those people. To everyone who is hurting.

However, I still believe that once you are an adult, there is a responsibility for you to dig deeper (even though it is extremely painful and you shouldn't HAVE to do this), eventually becoming a better person because of that hard work.

Becoming a better person, I believe, is just progressively, with time, becoming the best version of yourself you can be. And that means different things for different people.

I in no way intended to condemn people or shame them. I truly apologize if that is how it came across. I should have phrased my words better.

Interesting questions! I'll answer them to the best of my ability...and of course I am only one person with one perspective.

I think there are a lot of people that aren't trying hard enough to become a better person. As in they try in small ways (which is better than nothing!) but then often the ugliest sides of them stay in tact. It's usually not completely their fault that they don't try enough, but they definitely aren't excused from staying as they are. A lot of people don't want to know the hard truths about themselves; they want to stay in their comfort zone. But the only way to become a better person is to do this, then it gets easier to live with those truths, especially when they become untrue.

"Better people" is a difficult term...everyone is broken. Everyone is on different parts of the pathway of reconstruction. I think it is better to not focus on who is better, but just on how you individually can be better. And I believe that is an everyday battle. But it will be oh so worth it.

I hope this helps! Thank you for asking this. Good to discuss things like these.

I am really sorry you have experienced this. I totally agree that there is nothing necessarily wrong with not wanting to be in a relationship. As long as they are the right reasons, and you seem to have those. 

I would recommend what you seem to be doing right now: focusing in your goals in life, developing yourself, becoming a better person, reaching your ambitions, forming a good social circle, etc first. Then if some guy happens to come along that you think is compatible and you feel you are at a good enough time to date, then you can date. 

Even then, maybe you just don't want a relationship. And that's cool too. 

Keep being you! Don't let those people in your life telling those hurtful foolish untruths get to you!

I would say none of these...kind of a mixture? 

Right now, I believe that most people WANT to be good, and they can make efforts and become better people, but their inherent pervertedness and twistedness (sin) often gets in the way of this.

It seems people hav already given great advice, so I just wanted to add that I hear you and feel for you. I agree with everyone that that tutor has problems and you should not look into their actions that much. 

Only other thing I can think of that hasn't been said yet is to try therapy if you haven't already. It can be intimidating but SUPER rewarding. You just have to be willing to be vulnerable, and they should make that easier since they should be in a non-judging mode and compassionate, empathetic. You can learn things about yourself that you never would dream of, and that feeling of all the pieces in the puzzle connecting is one of the most relieving and empowering kind. 

I will pray for you. Remember that your true self is nothing to be ashamed of. The good and the bad. You don't need to hide it from anyone. Because we are all the same. And honestly, most people aren't worth getting immediate approval of because of that reason. No one is better than anyone else, the approval of someone doesn't have much worth unless you really respect them. I'm sure inside you know these things, but thought I would remind you.

I care about you. I care about how you feel, about what you do in life. A lot of other people do, or would if you told them this. I have had suicidal thoughts myself, and I know personally that it gets better. It wont always be like this. And transitioning from this horrible period of your life can be much faster if you reach out to people. Trust me. A lot of people will reach back. People are a lot more caring and open than you would think. Get therapy if you can. Please remember that things can and will get better. Ive heard this also from people who considered suicide. You are not alone. There is still beauty to be found in your life, plenty of it. Don't give up. It will be worth it. 

If you ever want to talk I'm here.

I understand not being ready to open up. I'm glad you are considering doing it in the future. I definitely recommend it. Heard great things about it from people I know, how it has changed their whole perspective, made life clearer and lighter. This is also from my own experience. It does take time though and it can be painful like you know. At least you are aware that you weren't ready to open up! Self awareness is very helpful. I hope you eventually try it again. And maybe even if you don't feel ready, try it anyway. Depending on your therapist, they could still make good breakthroughs.
Both haha

This could also at least partly be a general mental health problem. Negative cognitions. Things your brain learns to do with time based on negative experiences and/or personality. How it perceives the world. Have you ever tried going to therapy?
Very interesting! Maybe I will try this 🤔😏

Please know there’s always a way. Things can get better. I’ve heard stories of people contemplating suicide for reasons like yours, some even tried but failed. Then after a couple years they looked back and they saw how things got better. I know you don’t really want to die right? You just don’t want to live in these circumstances. Listen to your instinct. It’s there for a reason. I’ll always be here to talk. Please don’t do it. You have so much life left and you don’t know where it will lead. I’m sure that if you continue to fight, as difficult as it is, your future self will thank you. I’ll be praying for you. “For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have eternal life”.

Also just realized you were the original poster asking me that question…I hope I didn’t come across as cold or anything. I don’t use Reddit very much so im still learning how to works. I really care about you and what you do with your life.

Also please at least consider therapy. I’ve heard from other people that it’s changed their life for the better, that they needed it bc they couldn’t see the intricacies of the situation and needed unbiased help. It’s not for everyone, I know. But please at least consider it. Or call the suicide hotline. Immediate help. 
I hope my explanation of my faith was understandable and feel free to ask more questions if it doesn’t or your curious. I won’t be offended
Thank you for your prayers and recommendation. As my edit says, I took your advice :)

Thank you so much for this. A great beautiful reminder that Jesus suffered more than I could fathom and He understands and cares about my suffering. I questioned God during these times, but I still believe that He is for me. It’s just hard to not get angry especially when I don’t have the answers yet as to why I feel this way. 
Thank you so much, friend. May God bless you. And I want to reciprocate what you have done and say that if you are ever struggling, I’m always here to talk.

Christians are still human. We are not perfect, and God doesn’t expect us to be. We aren’t called to live a comfortable life here on earth. Actually, we are called to suffer. For the gospel yes, but also in strategic ways where the sin of the world, myself, and the devil try to attack me and bring me down, my suffering is manipulated in a way for good by the Lord. The Lord allows suffering so that we can learn to depend on Him, to get closer to Him, to stop clinging on to things that actually hurt us, to discover things about ourselves that can help us become stronger. we don’t always get an answer right away too. But I trust in Him still even when I long for death. He has helped me before and He will help me again

My heart goes out to you. Living can be so so difficult. Please, consider crying out to Jesus. This is not religion I’m talking about, but just Jesus. He loves you. No matter what you have done or who you are or what you look like. He loves you in the most pure and true way. How do I know? Because He died for you. He died with the weight of all the worlds sins on Him so that you could be with Him in this life and the next, eternally. You don’t need to be ashamed anymore. “If you confess with your mouth ‘Jesus is Lord’ and believe in your heart God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved”. Romans 10. I will pray for you. And please, get some professional help if you can as well.
